info.title: Euler Data API (V3)
info.description:
API specification for Euler Data v3. This spec defines the current
resource-oriented contract for the platform, with emphasis on consistent
schemas, predictable REST semantics, caching, observability, and a uniform
developer experience.

This public document covers unauthenticated endpoints and integrations that
use API keys, including capability-scoped keys. Browser-session Toolbox
operations, admin-secret operations, and the Prometheus endpoint are served
separately and are intentionally omitted.

Migration notes
- Euler Data v3 is not a path-for-path clone of v1/v2. Some endpoints map
  directly, some require multiple v3 calls, and some legacy aggregates were
  intentionally removed.
- The live [migration guide](/v3/docs/migration) explains how legacy v1/v2
  endpoints and payloads map into the v3 resource model.
- Important semantic changes:
  - Vault base APY and rewards APY are exposed separately in v3.
  - Account positions are flattened into account-vault rows instead of the
    legacy nested sub-account shape.
  - All supported API paths live under `/v3`; legacy paths return `410`.
  - Summary endpoints prefer smaller, focused resources over large
    BFF-style payloads.

Base path: /v3

Conventions
- JSON field naming: camelCase
- Addresses: accept lowercase or checksum; responses are EIP-55 checksummed
- Public APY values (`*Apy`, `apy*`): percent numbers with 6 decimal places (e.g., 5.123456 = 5.123456%)
- Contract interest-rate fields (`borrowAPY`, `supplyAPY` in `interestRates`): decimal strings in contract fraction units
- Ratios (utilization, LTV, etc.): numbers with 6 decimal places
- Response timestamps: ISO-8601 strings (UTC). Some legacy fields still expose unix
  seconds for compatibility and include `*Iso` companions.
- Query time ranges: unix seconds (from/to)

Unit policy
- v3 separates market metadata from contract verdicts by both name and type.
- Market-normalized USD prices and USD values are JSON numbers. These are values
  derived from off-chain pricing, cached price snapshots, or API-level market math.
  This includes `/v3/prices`, token price routes, vault/earn/protocol USD totals,
  portfolio market values, portfolio USD liquidation/risk fields such as
  `liabilityValueUsd`, `totalCollateralValueUsd`, `borrowLiquidationPriceUsd`,
  and `collateralLiquidationPricesUsd`, and vault holder `assetsUsd`.
- Contract-derived oracle and raw account-liquidity verdict values are exact strings.
  These preserve the integer value used by contracts, normalized to 18 decimals
  for API exposure. Oracle prices are quoted in the vault unit of account, which
  can be USD, ETH, or another asset. This includes `/v3/oracles/prices`, raw
  account-liquidity `liabilityValue` and `totalCollateralValue` objects,
  `liabilityValueBorrowing`, `liabilityValueLiquidation`, and collateral verdict
  values.
- On-chain token quantities are bigint strings in their native unit scale. This
  includes amounts, balances, shares, assets, borrows, reward amounts, liquidation
  repay/yield amounts, and block numbers.
- Caps are also bigint strings, but EVK caps are exposed as resolved underlying
  asset-unit amounts rather than packed contract config words; an unlimited EVK cap is
  type(uint256).max and `0` is a zero cap. The exceptions are
  cap-history and config-history, which carry the raw uint16 encodings.
- LTV config values use canonical basis-point strings. Legacy decimal aliases
  may remain on config-history payloads for compatibility when explicitly named.

Rate limiting
- Optional API keys for higher limits
- Standard limits are 1000 req/min for unauthenticated callers (IP-based)
  and 10000 req/min for authenticated callers (per API key), with a 60s window.
  Individual API keys can carry a custom limit.
- By default, proxy headers are not trusted for IP identity unless explicitly enabled.
- Redis failures default to fail-closed (503) for strict enforcement; fail-open is opt-in.
- RateLimit-* (IETF draft-6) and legacy X-RateLimit-* headers are returned.

CORS
- Public API responses use wildcard CORS, including preflight responses for unsafe methods.
- Unsafe methods with request bodies must use a JSON media type.

Caching
- Cache-Control headers are returned for cacheable endpoints.
- Defaults (may be adjusted in config):
  - Prices: 300s
  - APYs: 600s
  - Rewards: 900s
  - General responses: 60s (short 30s, long 300s)

Errors
- All errors use a standard envelope: { error: { code, message, requestId, details? } }
- Domain error codes are documented in this spec.
- Each chain lists the capabilities this deployment runs for it in `/v3/chains`. An operation
  that needs one names it in `x-chain-capability`; a chain without it answers
  `404 CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED` with `details.chainIds` and `details.capability`, never
  empty data. A read across chains that names no `chainId` leaves such chains out and lists
  them in `meta.excludedChains`.
- JSON request bodies must use `Content-Type: application/json` or another `application/*+json` media type.
- Request bodies larger than 1 MiB are rejected before route parsing with `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`.

tags.name: Protocol
tags.description: Protocol-wide summary endpoints and aggregate metrics. In v3, these endpoints are explicitly summary-oriented and should be treated as lightweight rollups rather than replacements for full vault list payloads.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness, readiness, and dashboard-friendly platform status checks. Public readiness calls use a bounded per-process admission budget; dependency-health routes share that budget and Kubernetes probes use a Service-excluded management listener. Use these for operational monitoring, not for reconstructing full portfolio state.

tags.name: Labels
tags.description:
The labeling system behind the Toolbox: entity and product profiles, vault labels, vault assessments, geo policies, and label publishing. The address that governs a vault is its governing address: the governor of an EVK or Securitize vault, the owner of an Earn vault. In this API "controller" always means the EVC controller, the liability vault an account has enabled through the Ethereum Vault Connector, never the address that governs a vault.

**Errors on the `/v3/labels` routes.** Key on the status, `error.code` and `error.details.reason`; `error.message` is for people and may change. `details.cause` narrows a reason that has several causes. An error without a reason is the only one its route answers with that status and code. The labels routes never answer `SERVICE_DISABLED`.

| Status | Code | `details.reason` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 401 | UNAUTHORIZED | `invalid-session` | No active session of a kind the route accepts. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `authorization-denied` | The actor may not make this write. `details.cause`: `platform-admin-denied`, `missing-csrf` or `csrf-mismatch` on platform-only routes; `wrong-entity`, `insufficient-role`, `unsupported-actor`, `inactive-actor`, `malformed-actor` or `missing-actor` on entity, member, address, product and vault writes. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `missing-csrf`, `csrf-mismatch` | Entity-or-platform route, unsafe method: the CSRF header is missing or does not match. While a session changes under the request the reason can also be `missing-session`, `invalid-session`, `expired-session`, `entity-member-denied`, `entity-auth-disabled` or `platform-admin-denied`. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `entity-suspended` | The member's entity is suspended by the platform. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `entity-admin-required` | The route needs an entity admin; the session is an editor. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `entity-scope-denied` | A draft read of another entity's rows. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `self-demotion-denied`, `self-revoke-denied` | An entity admin demoting or revoking their own membership. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `published-row` | An entity member deleting a product the public has seen. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `ungoverned-locked` | An ungoverned vault or product is write-once for entity members. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `ownership-denied` | No entity address governs the vault; on a product, `details.addresses` lists the vaults the entity no longer governs. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `vault-not-claimable` | An escrow vault, or a vault type an entity cannot claim. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `no-governing-address` | The vault has no governor or owner on chain (`details.role`); only Euler can assign it. |
| 403 | FORBIDDEN | `capability-denied`, `api-key-read-only`, `platform-session-required` | An API key without the capability, a key on a write a read grant cannot make, or an action only a platform session may take. |
| 404 | NOT_FOUND | `unknown-vault` | The vault is not in indexed factory discovery. |
| 404 | NOT_FOUND | `label-set-not-found`, `label-version-not-found`, `hold-not-found`, `resource-not-found` | Label set, version, hold and quarantine routes. |
| 404 | NOT_FOUND | none | The entity, member, address, product, vault labels or listing override does not exist. On the label reads, a 404 with `details.labelSet` and `details.version` means the label set or version could not be resolved; only that 404 carries `details.labelSet`. |
| 404 | CHAIN_NOT_SUPPORTED | none | A product or vault delete or transfer on a chain the deployment does not serve. |
| 404 | CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED | none | A product or vault delete or transfer, or a listing override, on a served chain without labels; `details.chainIds` and `details.capability: labels`. A write naming such a chain in its body or path answers 422 naming `chainId`. |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `duplicate` | The entity, address, product or vault labels already exist. |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `already-member`, `email-unavailable` | Adding a member: the email is already an active member of this entity (`details.memberId`), or another entity holds it (only a platform session also gets `details.entityId` and `details.revokedAt`). |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `address-taken` | The address is registered to another entity (`details.holderEntityId`). |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `already-revoked`, `last-active-admin-denied` | The member is already revoked, or the change would leave the entity without an active admin. |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `referenced` | Entity delete while products, claimed vaults or co-brands reference it (`details.references`). |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `vault-type-mismatch`, `mixed-governance`, `invalid-membership` | The vault type differs from discovery (`details.actualType`), the product would mix governed and ungoverned vaults, or a vault type cannot belong to a product (`details.addresses`). |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `already-quarantined`, `already-released`, `entity-hold` | Hold routes; an entity hold is released by resuming the entity. |
| 409 | CONFLICT | `label-set-not-publishable`, `version-exists`, `publication-suspended`, `restore-conflict` | Publishing and restoring label versions. |
| 412 | PRECONDITION_FAILED | none | `If-Match` names an older `updatedAt`; `details.updatedAt` is the current one. |
| 412 | PRECONDITION_FAILED | `draft-changed` | A publish's `expectedDraftToken` no longer matches its dry run; `details.draftToken` is the current one. |
| 412 | PRECONDITION_FAILED | `stale-review` | A hold or release whose `expectedContentHash` no longer matches the draft row; `details.contentHash` is the current one, and nothing is written. |
| 503 | SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE | `publication-in-progress` | A publication holds the label set; retry after `Retry-After` (5 seconds). |
| 503 | SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE | `ownership-unavailable`, `governance-unavailable`, `capability-check-unavailable` | On-chain ownership, product governance or an API key capability could not be checked. |
| 400 | BAD_REQUEST, VALIDATION_ERROR, INVALID_ADDRESS, INVALID_CHAIN_ID | none | Malformed JSON or filter (`details.param`), a malformed `If-Match`, or a malformed address or chain id in the path. |
| 422 | VALIDATION_ERROR | none | Body or query validation; `details.issues[]` names each `path`. |
| 413, 415, 429 | PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED | none | A body over 1 MiB, a body that is not JSON, or a rate limit (`Retry-After`). |

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: API usage and API key analytics. These endpoints are intended for operators and consumers tracking traffic, rate limits, and key-level activity.

tags.name: Images
tags.description: Stable, extensionless image URLs and the authenticated image catalog used by Euler applications.

tags.name: Changes
tags.description: Change requests for managed data. Every data area (token images, price sources, and later ones) goes through the same routes, with server-side checks, a per-domain policy that applies or proposes, admin review, revert, and an auto-apply kill switch.

tags.name: Chains
tags.description: Chain inventory and per-chain protocol summaries. These replace ad-hoc chain-level aggregates from legacy APIs with explicit, cacheable resources.

tags.name: Vaults
tags.description: Canonical vault resources, vault history, holders, borrowers, and open-interest views. In v3, vault detail is decomposed into focused endpoints instead of one large legacy response.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: Account activity, discovered positions, and sub-account relationships. Legacy nested account payloads are flattened into account-vault rows in v3.

tags.name: Activity
tags.description: Normalized vault and owner event timelines with explicit per-chain source coverage and cursor pagination.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: Token metadata, protocol classifications, and related static reference data used throughout the API.

tags.name: Prices
tags.description: Current and historical token prices. Prices follow v3 source priority rules, return the canonical merged value, and expose provenance only as `onchain`, `offchain`, or `hardcoded`. Current-price responses are best-known observations up to 7 days old; clients use `timestamp` to evaluate age. `timestamp` is the provider's own time for the price when it gives one (CoinGecko `last_updated_at`, DefiLlama `timestamp`, Pyth `publish_time`; an ERC-4626 share takes its underlying's), and the time V3 read it otherwise (Pendle, the on-chain fallback), so a quote the provider stopped updating ages like any other. Derived USD calculations never use observations older than 24 hours. A price from a source set up per token (Pyth, Pendle, CoinGecko, DefiLlama, ERC-4626) is served only while the token has an enabled entry for that source. The on-chain fallback prices a vault asset with no entry by itself, and a token's `onchain` entry changes that. Enabled with an oracle adapter address, the token's on-chain price is that adapter's quote, with no assessment. The admin who pinned it vouches for it. If the quote fails, the token gets no on-chain price. Enabled with `any`, it quotes through any assessed adapter. Disabled, the token gets no on-chain price and its stored one stops being served. A share priced through it gets no new on-chain quote, but its stored one is served until it ages unless the share's own entry is disabled too. After any change to the entry, a fallback price read before the change is not served. A price-source change takes effect at once, since the token's cached price is dropped.

tags.name: APYs
tags.description: Base and intrinsic APY surfaces. In v3, APY families are split into dedicated endpoints instead of being embedded inconsistently across larger payloads.

tags.name: Rewards
tags.description: Reward campaign APRs and per-account reward breakdowns. Rewards APY is intentionally separate from base vault APY in v3; combine them client-side when you need a legacy-style total supply APY.

tags.name: Oracles
tags.description: Oracle routing, adapter, and price-source inspection endpoints. Price provenance is exposed only as `onchain`, `offchain`, or `hardcoded`.

tags.name: Earn
tags.description: Euler Earn vault resources and historical data. These endpoints are separate from EVK vaults and should be modeled independently in client code.

tags.name: Securitize
tags.description: Securitize collateral vaults, which the Securitize factory deploys and the issuer governs. Separate from the EVK routes, which never list them.

tags.name: Liquidations
tags.description: Liquidation events and related historical views used for risk analysis and monitoring.

tags.name: TermsOfUse
tags.description: Terms-of-use signature state and audit endpoints.

tags.name: EVC
tags.description: Ethereum Vault Connector account event resources. These are separate from account position snapshots and are intended for event-level inspection.

tags.name: PublicAllocator
tags.description: Public allocator event resources for allocator-level activity and history.

tags.name: FeeFlow
tags.description: Fee-flow event resources and fee-related historical activity.

tags.name: GraphQL
tags.description: Controlled GraphQL passthrough endpoints for indexer-backed data exploration and compatibility workflows.

tags.name: Compliance
tags.description: Capability-gated address screening for trusted server-side consumers.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key authentication (optional; higher rate limits).

BearerAuth.description: Alternative to X-API-Key using Authorization: Bearer <key>

X-Label-Set.description: The label set this read resolved, for example `public`.

X-Label-Version.description: The label version this read resolved. For a published read it is the version's key (`latest`, `production` and other aliases resolve to it, for example `v20260929144948869`); send it back as `version=` to pin later reads to the same snapshot. For a `current` or `draft` read it is `draft`.

X-Label-Version-Id.description: The resolved published version's id. Absent on `current` and `draft` reads. It is not accepted as a `version=` selector; pin on `X-Label-Version`.

AssessmentETag.description: The assessment's `platformUpdatedAt` in double quotes; absent while the vault has no stored assessment. Send it back as `If-Match` on the next PATCH.

ImageVersionQuery.name: v
ImageVersionQuery.description: First 8 hex characters of the image's content digest, as `logoURI` carries it. Only the current digest earns the year-long immutable cache; any other value, a malformed one included, is ignored and the image is served with the one-hour cache, never an error.

WorkItemIdPath.name: id
WorkItemIdPath.description: Work item ID as listed, `<chainId>:<token address>`.

ChainIdParam.name: chainId
ChainIdParam.description: Comma-separated list of positive chain IDs (single value allowed). Duplicate IDs are removed in first-occurrence order; at most 20 distinct IDs and 512 input characters are accepted.

RewardsBreakdownChainIdParam.name: chainId
RewardsBreakdownChainIdParam.description:
Optional comma-separated chain filter. Every element must be a positive
safe integer; surrounding whitespace is ignored, and empty elements are
invalid. Duplicate IDs are accepted, count once toward the fan-out limit,
and preserve first-occurrence order. At most 12 distinct supported chain
IDs are allowed. Omitting this parameter leaves the result unrestricted by
chain.

AddressScreeningHistoryChainParam.name: chain
AddressScreeningHistoryChainParam.description: Matches the requested or resolved chain of an evaluation, or the chain of a request.

AddressScreeningHistoryFromParam.name: from
AddressScreeningHistoryFromParam.description: Inclusive lower bound on the evaluation or request time (RFC 3339).

AddressScreeningHistoryToParam.name: to
AddressScreeningHistoryToParam.description: Inclusive upper bound on the evaluation or request time (RFC 3339).

AddressScreeningEvaluationSuspiciousPara.name: suspicious
AddressScreeningEvaluationSuspiciousPara.description:
`true` for the evaluations that flagged the address, `false` for the
clear ones; absent for both. Applied before paging, so `meta.total`
counts the matching evaluations.

OffsetParam.name: offset
OffsetParam.description: Page offset, capped at 10000 to bound query cost.

IndexedEventsOffsetParam.name: offset
IndexedEventsOffsetParam.description: Indexed-event page offset as a non-negative base-10 safe integer, with a maximum of 1000. Invalid values are rejected; use narrower time or event-type filters for deeper history.

AccountPositionsOffsetParam.name: offset
AccountPositionsOffsetParam.description: Account-position page offset, capped at 1000 to bound position discovery and enrichment work.

LimitParam.name: limit
LimitParam.description: Requested page size. Values above the endpoint cap are clamped; the default shared cap is 100.

LabelViewParam.name: view
LabelViewParam.description: Read view. `curation` (default) returns raw label fields with the resolved block nested, mirroring the write schema so read-modify-write round-trips stay safe. `resolved` returns the display cascade flattened to the top level with raw fields omitted, for read-only consumers. Unknown values are rejected with 400.

LabelVersionParam.name: version
LabelVersionParam.description: Version selector. Omission, `latest`, and `production` select the latest published snapshot. Explicit `current` and `draft` select the mutable working copy and require an authorized session as documented by the endpoint. Other published keys and aliases retain their stored casing.

TokenLimitParam.name: limit
TokenLimitParam.description: Requested token page size. Values above 500 are clamped.

IncludeParam.name: include
IncludeParam.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to expand. Unknown values are ignored.

SortParam.name: sort
SortParam.description: Sort field, prefix with '-' for descending.

HistoryFromParam.name: from
HistoryFromParam.description: Unix timestamp in seconds, no later than 2038-01-19T03:14:07Z.

HistoryToParam.name: to
HistoryToParam.description: Unix timestamp in seconds, no later than 2038-01-19T03:14:07Z.

address.description: Hook target address for hook-target entries; vault address for rule-exemption entries; oracle adapter address for custom-adapter and adapter-check-exemption entries.

ruleKey.description: Exempted finding key (rule-exemption entries only), e.g. `collateral.0x....ltv`; for adapter-check-exemption entries, the adapter health check key that is accepted.

fingerprint.description: Metadata-stripped runtime bytecode SHA-256 (custom-adapter entries only).

sessionBound.description: Custom-adapter entries only: the reviewed adapter pauses outside trading sessions. A quote revert on one of its routed pairs is then excused (`not_applicable`) when that pair quoted successfully within `maxSilenceSeconds`, measured from the last successful quote v3 observed on the pair. A pair silent longer, or never seen quoting, still fails.

maxSilenceSeconds.description: Set exactly when `sessionBound`; between 3600 and 604800 (seven days, the closure bound of the modeled session-bound adapters).

updatedAt.description: When the row last changed. Rows written before it was recorded carry their creation time.

version.description: `toolbox:<updatedAt>`; the `expectedVersion` of a `trust-entries` change. Trust entries are never edited in place, so it moves only when the entry is replaced.

RowAuthor.description: Who wrote the row: a platform admin by id, or a system actor such as `admin-secret` or `euler-labels-unified-importer`. Shown only to a platform session whose operator is on the Toolbox admin allowlist; null for every other reader, and for rows written before authors were recorded.

code.description:
Domain error code. Examples:
- BAD_REQUEST
- INVALID_ADDRESS
- INVALID_CHAIN_ID
- CHAIN_NOT_SUPPORTED
- CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED
- NOT_FOUND
- VAULT_NOT_FOUND
- TOKEN_NOT_FOUND
- ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND
- VALIDATION_ERROR
- CONFLICT
- PRECONDITION_FAILED
- PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE
- RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
- UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE
- UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT
- UNAUTHORIZED
- FORBIDDEN
- SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
- SERVICE_DISABLED
- INTERNAL_ERROR

details.description: Context of the error. Where present, `details.reason` is a stable kebab-case value to key on, and `details.cause` narrows a reason that has several causes. The labels routes list theirs in the Labels tag.

aliases.description: Named selectors for this version. `latest` is carried by exactly one published version per label set, the one `isLatest` marks: a publish hands it over from the previous version in the same transaction.

checksum.description: SHA-256 checksum of canonical entity, product, and vault-label content, the server-derived `isEscrow` flag of a vault included. Audit timestamps and geo policies are excluded.

publishedByKind.description: Who created the version. The publisher's identity is platform-only and appears on the publication state route.

createdBy.description: Present for platform sessions; API keys see null.

createdByEmail.description: The email of the platform administrator `createdBy` names, for display. Present for platform sessions when the id is a known administrator; null otherwise and for API keys.

publishedBy.description: Platform administrator id, worker id, or API key id, matching `publishedByKind`. Present for platform sessions; API keys see null.

publishedByEmail.description: The email of the platform administrator `publishedBy` names when `publishedByKind` is `platform-admin`, for display. Present for platform sessions; null for the worker, for keys, and for API key sessions.

publishedChanges.description: Change-log rows this version carried; present on the version history.

suspended.description: Automatic publication is suspended (relevant in `scheduled` mode).

dueAt.description: When the pending draft is due in `scheduled` mode; null when nothing is pending or the mode is `manual`.

mode.description: How changes go live. `manual` (the rollout default): only an explicit publish by a platform session or a key with `labels:publish` creates a version; no publication window opens and `dueAt` stays null (a CHECK enforces it). `scheduled`: label writes open a window and the worker publishes after the cooldown. Changed in the database only; every mode change resets the schedule, so a switch to `scheduled` opens nothing until the next label write, and a switch to `manual` disarms an open window.

suspended.description: A platform actor has suspended automatic publication (relevant in `scheduled` mode). Explicit publication still works.

id.description: Present for platform sessions; API keys see the kind only.

frozenByEnvironment.description: The deployment override (`LABEL_PUBLICATION_FROZEN`) is set. Lifting it is a deploy, not an API call.

effectiveFrozen.description: True when either the suspension or the environment override stops the timer. In `manual` mode there is no timer; explicit publication is unaffected either way.

minDelaySeconds.description: Cooldown after the last label change before the timer publishes. At least 60.

maxDelaySeconds.description: Cap from the first unpublished change; the timer publishes at the latest here. At most 86400.

dueAt.description: When the pending draft is due, or null when nothing is pending or the mode is `manual`.

revision.description: Identifies the pending mutations; increments with every scheduled label write.

controlOutcome.description: Whether this request changed the state or found it already as requested.

publishOutcome.description: Whether this request created a snapshot or returned the unchanged latest snapshot.
What the same request without `dryRun` would do.

changes.description: What publishing would change, row by row: the report's `published` and `pulledIn` rows with their content on both sides, then the `heldBack` rows (`held: true`) with the draft content a lifted hold would publish. This is the exact answer to "what would publishing change", computed by the same comparison publication uses, so it covers every difference between the draft and the latest version, including writes the change log never sees.

draftToken.description: Opaque token for exactly what this preview would publish, including the holds a partial publish would override. Send it back as `expectedDraftToken` to publish only if nothing moved since.

held.description: True for a row a hold keeps out of this publication: it is listed in the report's `heldBack`, is not taken, and its `after` is the draft content the hold keeps out.

before.description: The complete row as the latest published version carries it, in the published shape (every published field, no timestamps or assignment); null for a create.

after.description: The complete row as the new version would carry it (for a held row, as the draft has it), in the published shape; null for a delete.

changedFields.description: The fields whose value differs between `before` and `after`, sorted.

LabelRowKey.description: Identifies one publishable row across the draft and every version.

LabelRowSelection.description: The rows a partial publish takes from the draft. Dependencies the selected rows need are pulled in automatically; everything else keeps its published content. Platform sessions only.

action.description: `restore` marks a row a whole-draft restore brought back; `scoped-restore` one that a restore limited to a curator, products or vaults brought back; `transfer` a row the platform moved to another curator.

initialAction.description: The action the row first waited with. A later write to the same row supersedes its pending change and carries this forward, so a claim followed by an edit still reads as a claim until it is published. Equals `action` when nothing was superseded.

afterContentHash.description: Hash of `after` as a draft row; null when the change deleted the row. On a row's `pending` or `quarantined` change it is the current draft row's hash: send it as a hold's or release's `expectedContentHash`.

LabelHoldSummary.description: What a draft read shows on a held row.

id.description: Returned to platform sessions only; keys see null.

email.description: The platform administrator's email, for display next to the id. Returned to platform sessions only; null for keys, the system, and key sessions.

LabelHold.description: A row held out of publication. A quarantine is a rejection of one row; an entity hold is raised by entity suspension and covers every row the entity owns. Held rows keep their published content on every full publish while the draft stays intact.

contentHash.description: Hash of the draft row when the hold was raised; null when the draft lacked the row.

releaseReason.description: Why the hold was released, when the release gave a reason: a quarantine release, or the entity resume that lifted an entity hold. Null while the hold is active.

reason.description: Why the hold is released or the entity resumed. Trimmed; blank or null records no reason.

expectedContentHash.description: The draft revision the reviewer judged: the change log's `afterContentHash` for the row (null for a row the draft no longer has). Compared with the current draft row inside the write's transaction; when the row moved since, the answer is 412 with `details.reason` `stale-review` and the current `details.contentHash`, and nothing is written. Optional for now; keys will have to send it, and a key write without it is logged.

The draft revision the reviewer judged: the change log's `afterContentHash` for the row (null for a row the draft no longer has). Compared with the current draft row inside the write's transaction; when the row moved since, the answer is 412 with `details.reason` `stale-review` and the current `details.contentHash`, and nothing is written. Optional for now; keys will have to send it, and a key write without it is logged.

LabelPublicationReport.description: What the snapshot builder did: `published` rows went live from the draft, `pulledIn` rows were needed by a selected row, `heldBack` rows carry a pending change a hold kept out (their own hold, a held dependency absent from the published version, or a held published row that still needs them), and `overrides` are held rows the selection published anyway.

leftOut.description: Draft vault rows with no labels (the rows discovery materialises for vaults nobody claimed, claims cleared), which the publication leaves out: how many the draft holds, and which of them the selection named, a no-op rather than an error. A selection naming only such rows answers `publishOutcome: unchanged` with them listed here.

logo.description: Absolute https URL or a safe asset filename without path separators.

riskMethodology.description: Markdown, at most 16384 characters, stored trimmed; link destinations must be http(s) or relative.

security.description: Markdown, at most 16384 characters, stored trimmed; link destinations must be http(s) or relative.

termsOfService.description: Markdown, at most 16384 characters, stored trimmed; link destinations must be http(s) or relative.

licenses.description: Markdown, at most 16384 characters, stored trimmed; link destinations must be http(s) or relative.

disclaimers.description: Markdown, at most 16384 characters, stored trimmed; link destinations must be http(s) or relative.

hold.description: The hold covering this row on a draft read; absent on published reads.

suspendedAt.description: Draft reads only; absent on published reads.

suspensionReason.description: Draft reads by platform sessions only.

memberCount.description: Active (not revoked) members. Present only on `GET /v3/labels/entities?include=counts`.

adminCount.description: Active members with the admin role; zero means nobody can manage the team. Present only on `GET /v3/labels/entities?include=counts`.

addressCount.description: Registered entity addresses. Present only on `GET /v3/labels/entities?include=counts`.

EntityAddress.description:
A verified address of a KYBed entity. Addresses are chain-agnostic: one
registration proves that the entity owns the address on every
supported chain. The address set is the ownership evidence for vault
claims; a claim is still verified per vault against that vault's
governor at a pinned block. One address belongs to at most one entity.

address.description: EIP-55 checksummed verified address in API responses.

label.description: Optional human-readable label. Editable by entity admins and platform admins.

PriceCoverageWorkItem.description: One in-scope asset on the token-price-missing work list.

id.description: Opaque work item ID, `<chainId>:<lowercase token address>`.

state.description: `reviewed` while an applied review stands (see `review.kind`). Otherwise, first match wins: `unpriced` (no eligible price within 24 hours, or never), `aging` (newest price older than 12 hours), `source-stopped` (a fresh price exists but a configured source failed recent runs), `onchain-only` (only the on-chain fallback is fresh) and `priced`. Only served prices count: a source set up per token counts only while the token has an enabled entry for it. Listed items are never `priced`; a dismiss or resume response can be.

since.description: When the asset entered its state, derived from price and source timestamps; for a reviewed item, the review time. An asset never priced counts from its catalog entry.

price.description: Last known served price with its internal source name, of any age: fresh sources by precedence, otherwise the newest stale one.

stale.description: True when the price is older than 24 hours.

sources.description: Configured and observed price sources. Each orchestrator run stores only the highest-ranked source with a fresh quote for the token (the newest quote when none is fresh), in the write-time merge order erc4626-fixed < erc4626 < defillama < coingecko < pendle < pyth. So a configured source silent for 24 hours, or never seen, is `stopped` or `never` only when the fresh winner ranks below it; it is `outranked` when a higher-ranked source won, and its health is then unknown. A source set up per token that the token has no enabled entry for is `stopped`, whatever the age of its last row: V3 no longer serves it. So is the on-chain fallback of a token whose `onchain` entry is disabled.

fallback.description: Latest on-chain fallback outcome, read for up to 26 hours. When `outcome` is `priced`, the fallback stored that price. Otherwise it gives the reason for the first step that failed, for example `out-of-scope` (only adapters of vaults the app does not show could price it), `reference-required` (a fixed or rate-provider adapter without an independent reference) or `assessment-warning` (every candidate adapter has failing checks).

depositsRaw.description: Deposits of the asset in in-scope vaults, in base units.

review.description: The open review, if any. It stays on the item after it lapses (a later price ruled it out), for context; `state` then shows the computed state instead of `reviewed`.

unreadSources.description: Price sources whose token list could not be read. While it is not empty, the list is partial, because entries of these sources are missing from each item's `sources`.

counts.description: Listed items on the requested chains, before the state filter and paging.

WorkItemReview.description: The applied review that moved a work item off the outstanding list.

changeId.description: The applied change that records the review.

kind.description: The recognized terminal state, or null for a plain dismissal (stop looking for now). `onchain-only` or `no-price-source` on `token-price-missing`; `no-logo-available` on `token-logo-missing`; `no-category` on `token-category-missing` and `no-intrinsic-apy` on `token-intrinsic-apy-missing`, which take no null kind; `no-rule-needed` on `asset-newly-exposed`, where a null-kind review lapses when the asset is exposed again after it. A price item with a null-kind review is `reviewed` and lapses like `no-price-source`: any price observed after the decision brings it back. A logo item with a null-kind review stays reviewed until it is resumed.

decidedBy.description: The platform admin's email, else `<actorKind>:<actorId>`. Null for an API-key reader, which never sees operator identities.

ChangeActorRef.description: Who did it. API-key readers see only their own key's ID; every other actor is shown by kind with a null ID and label.

label.description: The platform admin's email or the key's name; null for API-key readers.

ChangeCheck.description: A check the server ran itself. A caller's claims are evidence, never checks.

decision.description: Null on rows recorded before the generic policy existed.

ChangeEvidence.description: Required from API keys and system actors. Reviewers see it; the policy never reads it.

ChangeRecord.description: One change in any data domain, with its full record.

opClass.description: What the change does, computed by the server. Geo changes are `tighten` (more people or assets fall under a rule), `loosen` (fewer, including any change that loosens one part) or `update` (nothing anyone is subject to changes, for example the reason).

value.description: The proposed after-state, in the domain's value shape.

before.description: The state when the change was submitted.

appliedValue.description: The state the change wrote, when applied.

uploadId.description: Token images only: the staged upload the change carries.

sourceProvider.description: Token images only: `coingecko`, `pendle` or `pendle-pt-ring`; null for an upload.

sourceEvidence.description: Token images only: the provider record or the derivation the image came from.

events.description: Present on the detail read only, oldest first.

details.description: What the event recorded. An API-key reader sees only `decision`, `stale`, `kind`, `reason`, `comment` and the related change ids, plus `error` as the generic `{ message: 'The change could not be applied' }`, as on the change itself.

sha256.description: The current managed image digest; send it as `expectedVersion`.

suppression.description: The applied removal or dismissal that keeps automatic sourcing off; null when sourcing is open.

ChangeSubmitRequest.description: The generic body for every domain. The server computes the operation class, runs its own checks and decides with the domain's policy.

key.description: The domain's target key, in the `keyFormat` that `GET /v3/changes/domains` serves: `<chainId>:<address>` for token images and for every dismissal or resume, `<source>/<chainId>:<address>` for price sources, `<tag>:<ruleType>:<value>` for token tags (rule types `symbols`, `symbolPrefixes`, `symbolContains`, `coingeckoCategories`, and `addresses`, whose value names one token as `<chainId>:<address>` in any case and is stored lowercase).

value.description: The proposed after-state in the domain's value shape (`valueSchema` in `GET /v3/changes/domains`); omitted or null for a removal or a dismissal without a kind. A `token-images` `derive` takes `{ source?: { chainId, address } }`.

expectedVersion.description: The version the caller read; null when the target is empty. A stale version supersedes the change. Read it from `GET /v3/changes/targets/{domain}?key=…` (or `GET /v3/changes/targets/price-sources/{chainId}/{address}` for every source of a token).

value.description: The current state in the domain's value shape; null while empty.

version.description: Send as `expectedVersion`; null while the target is empty.

history.description: Decided changes, newest first, at most 50.

entry.description: The configured entry (identifier, symbol, metadata, enabled).

version.description: Send as `expectedVersion` to change this entry.

capabilities.description: Null for a domain no key may change.

checks.description: Every check the domain can run on a change, by the `id` its change records use. A check that does not apply to an entry answers `skip` with the reason and `details.applies: false`.

purpose.description: One sentence on what the check protects.

relation.description: How the token is built on the other: in `parents` the other token is what this one wraps; in `reachedVia` the other token wraps this one.

strategies.description: An Earn vault's strategies, from its supply and withdraw queues.

GeoExposureSignals.description: Server-read facts about the token. A read that failed on the last attempt is named in `unavailable`.

proxy.description: The proxy the token is (EIP-1967, an EIP-1967 beacon or an EIP-1167 clone); null for a plain contract.

GeoExposureWorkItem.description: One asset on the asset-newly-exposed work list.

id.description: `<chainId>:<lowercase asset address>`, as on every work list.

state.description: The first that applies: `covered` (a geo rule applies on the whole chain), `reviewed` (a standing review), `baseline` (exposed when the chain's first sweep ran), `unverified-only` (reached only through vaults the app does not show, by holding or by lineage), `new`. Only `new` is outstanding. An `unverified-only` asset that a shown vault starts to reach becomes `new` on the next sweep.

priority.description: One step per order of magnitude of `depositsUsd` ($10 is 1, $10M is 7); 0 when unknown or below $1.

vaults.description: The vaults that hold the asset itself, shown in the app or not.

depositsRaw.description: Deposits of those vaults in the asset's base units.

depositsUsd.description: Deposits in USD at the last price, including the tokens built on the asset; null when no price is known.

parents.description: What the asset is built on.

reachedVia.description: The exposed tokens built on this asset, through which a vault reaches it.

fingerprints.description: The asset's proxy implementation as `implementation:0x…`, empty for a plain contract. A reviewer signal only: tokens that use the same implementation may come from one issuer or from a common template, and no rule covers a token through it. Code hashes are not recorded.

rules.description: Geo rules that cover the asset; on a `covered` item one of them applies on the whole chain, otherwise each applies only inside one product or vault.

AssetCoverageProposal.description: The oldest open proposal that addresses the piece, a proposed "none" review included; null when none does.

AssetCoverageReview.description: The standing review that settles or pauses the piece; null when none does.

kind.description: The review kind; null for a stop-for-now review, which pauses the piece.

settled.description: The piece has its data, an automatic match, or an applied "none" review. A settled piece is never a need.

need.description: Not settled, no open proposal, and the state is neither `out-of-scope` nor `paused`. The `needs` filter matches it.

AssetCoverage.description: The onboarding checklist of one exposed asset: logo, price, category (`tags`), intrinsic APY (`yield`) and geo. Logo, price, tags and yield apply only to assets shown in the app, the scope of the logo and price lists; any other asset has them as `out-of-scope`. Geo applies to every exposed asset. `paused` is a standing review without a kind (stop for now). Every piece is read in a batch for the page.

state.description: Settled: `present` (a managed image) or `none-reviewed` (an applied `no-logo-available` review).

Settled: `market` (a fresh market price), `onchain-only-reviewed` (an `onchain-only` review) or `none-reviewed` (a `no-price-source` review). The `token-price-missing` states `onchain-only`, `aging`, `source-stopped` and `unpriced` without a standing review are needs.

Intrinsic APY cannot be inferred, so every asset in scope needs a decision. Settled: `configured` (a provider wrote a non-zero intrinsic APY for the asset in the last 7 days, or an enabled entry exists and any provider wrote a row, zero included, in that time), `none-reviewed` (an applied `no-intrinsic-apy` review) or `not-applicable` (an Euler vault share: EVK, Earn, escrow or Securitize). `source-stopped` is a need: an enabled entry with no row for the asset in the last 7 days, a new entry included until its source first runs, or an asset whose only rows are older than 7 days. Only served rows count: a provider set up per token counts only while the asset has an enabled entry for it, and a DefiLlama pool row only while the enabled pool mapping names its pool.

sources.description: `yield-source`: an enabled yield-source entry; `yield-pool`: an enabled DefiLlama pool mapping; `provider`: a provider serves a non-zero intrinsic APY now.

state.description: Settled: `tagged` (any rule tags the token: a CoinGecko category, a symbol rule or an address rule) or `none-reviewed` (an applied `no-category` review). The proposal is a matching symbol, prefix, contains or address rule, or a proposed `no-category` review; category rules are not evaluated here.

tags.description: The tags `/v3/tokens` derives for the token.

state.description: Settled: `covered` (a geo rule applies on the whole chain) or `none-reviewed` (an applied `no-rule-needed` review). The proposal is a `geo` rule that names the asset address, or a proposed review of the asset.

counts.description: Items per state on the requested chains, before the state filter and paging.

kind.description: The work list's recognized terminal state, or null to stop for now. `no-rule-needed` is the `asset-newly-exposed` kind. `no-category` (`token-category-missing`) and `no-intrinsic-apy` (`token-intrinsic-apy-missing`) take no null.

TokenLogoWorkItem.description: One in-scope asset on the token-logo-missing work list.

id.description: Opaque work item ID, `<chainId>:<lowercase token address>`, as on every work list.

workerOutcome.description: The logo worker's latest outcome for the token: `no_candidate`, `invalid_source`, `provider_failure`, `created` or `already_present`. `shadow_candidate` is a legacy value the worker no longer writes; a token that still shows it is retried at `nextRetryAt`, and that attempt replaces it.

review.description: Null on the outstanding list; the applied dismissal on the reviewed list.

total.description: Exact total count when the endpoint provides one.

hasMore.description: Indicates whether another page exists beyond the current page.

limit.description: Echoed page size after endpoint-side clamping.

outcome.description: On a toolbox config DELETE, what happened to the row.

products.description: On a curation vault `POST`, `PUT`, or `PATCH`: the products the write touched (the one the vault left and the one it joined) as they are after the write, `governanceMode` included, so the caller applies them instead of re-reading.

chainId.description: Comma-separated chain IDs for multi-chain responses.

degradedProviders.description: Live providers whose data is incomplete in this response.

ExcludedChains.description: On a read across chains that names no `chainId`: the served chains it left out because they do not run the capability the operation needs, rather than reading them as empty. Absent when no chain was left out.

labeling.description: The chain accepts products, vault labels, and geo policies: `capabilities` includes `labels`. A client offers only rows with `labeling: true` in its label pickers. A label write naming a chain without labels answers 422 with a `details.issues[]` entry whose `path` is `["chainId"]`.

capabilities.description: What this deployment runs for the chain. `indexing` (the indexed reads) is always present; a route that needs a capability the chain lacks answers 404 `CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED` with `details.capability`.

logoURI.description: Chain logo URL, `/v3/images/chains/{chainId}` on the V3 image host. It depends on the chain id only, so a client can build it for chains this route does not list; keep a bundled logo as the fallback.

ProtocolStats.description: Lending aggregates across the selected chains, with Earn TVL reported separately.

totalSuppliedUsd.description: Total supplied in USD: the `cash + totalBorrows` of every counted EVK vault (escrow vaults included) plus the deposits of every counted Securitize vault (its shares outstanding, one share to one asset), valued in USD. Earn vault assets are excluded.

totalBorrowedUsd.description: Total borrows in USD of the counted EVK vaults, all borrows counted. Securitize and escrow vaults lend nothing.

earnTotalAssetsUsd.description: Total assets in USD of every counted Earn vault. Reported separately and not included in `totalSuppliedUsd` or `utilization`, since Earn deposits sit in EVK vaults.

utilization.description: Lending utilization, computed as `totalBorrowedUsd / totalSuppliedUsd`. Earn assets are excluded from the denominator.

vaultCount.description: The vaults whose value is in the totals: counted EVK, escrow, Securitize and Earn vaults, empty ones included. Vaults left out (not shown, hidden by Layer 1, not evaluated yet, without a usable price, or read too long ago) are not in it.

ProtocolStatsExcludedTotals.description: USD sums cover only the vaults among them that have a usable price.

suppliedUsd.description: EVK and Securitize supply these vaults would add to `totalSuppliedUsd`.

earnTotalAssetsUsd.description: Earn assets these vaults would add to `earnTotalAssetsUsd`.

ProtocolStatsExcludedVaults.description: Factory vaults the totals leave out on the included chains, by reason. Only vaults Layer 1 hides carry USD, valued from the same snapshot and price reads as the counted vaults; the others are counted only.

hiddenByLayer1.description: Vaults Layer 1 checks hide (`config-failed`, `config-suspended`, or a failed Layer 1 behind a Layer 2 hide). An escrow or Securitize vault a counted vault accepts as collateral keeps counting even when Layer 1 hides it. A hidden vault without a stored balance snapshot adds no USD.

notShown.description: Vaults the app does not show for any other reason: pending review or unclaimed, hidden by a platform admin or a curator verdict, delisted, or collateral no counted vault accepts.

notEvaluated.description: Vaults without a Layer 1 verdict yet.

unpriced.description: Counted vaults holding a balance without a usable price. Their USD is unknown.

stale.description: Counted vaults whose balance was read more than 15 minutes ago.

calculationTimestamp.description: Time at which chain availability and aggregates were evaluated.

complete.description: True when every chain in the requested scope with a counted vault contributed from fresh source state, with every counted vault's balance read. A vault without a usable price or with a balance read too long ago does not make its chain incomplete, however much of the chain it holds: it is left out of the totals and counted in `excludedVaults`. A chain is left out only when none of its counted vaults has a fresh balance (`stale_source`).

includedChainIds.description: Requested chains with counted vaults whose values contribute to the returned aggregate.

incompleteChainIds.description: Requested chains with incomplete membership, unread balances, or stale source state. A chain with only unread balances may still contribute the vaults it read.

incompleteChainReasons.description: Reasons for each incomplete chain in the requested scope. Empty for a complete response.

reasons.description: Null when the cached snapshot lacks reason provenance. `membership`: a counted vault is missing from the indexed inventory. `valuation`: a counted vault's balance could not be read; the chain still contributes the vaults it read. `stale_source`: none of the chain's counted vaults has a balance read in the last 15 minutes, priced or not, so nothing on the chain was observed. Every reason but `valuation` leaves the chain out of the totals.

excludedVaults.description: What the totals leave out and why, summed over the included chains. Null when an included chain's serving snapshot was written before this was recorded.

HistoryInterval.description: Inclusive UTC bucket-start bounds. A single absent bucket has equal from/to values.

availableBuckets.description: Distinct elapsed requested buckets with a finite value, including partial aggregate values and observed zero.

partialBuckets.description: Available buckets whose aggregate covers only part of the requested chain scope.

HistoryCoverage.description: Availability within the requested range, not proof of historical membership, vault inception, source retention, recoverability, or price accuracy. Leading and trailing absent buckets are included. Future buckets are excluded from evaluation; the current bucket is provisional. Missing fields and read failures remain unavailable without asserting their root cause.

status.description: Complete requires all evaluated buckets and all reported metrics. Missing means no returned buckets. Not applicable means the range is entirely in the future.

firstAvailable.description: First returned bucket within the evaluated range, not the earliest retained source date.

missingIntervals.description: Buckets absent from the response regardless of metric coverage.

metrics.description: Coverage keyed by public metric name. Available and missing bucket counts sum to evaluatedBuckets; partialBuckets is a subset of availableBuckets.

ProtocolHistoryPointCoverage.description: Coverage of the stored aggregate. Partially reconstructed chain rows can remain incomplete even when every requested chain has a stored row. Nullable Earn USD is reported separately; complete coverage does not certify every underlying historical source.

missingChainIds.description: Requested chain IDs without a row. Null for incomplete unfiltered days because the historical expected chain universe is not persisted.

timestamp.description: UTC start of the represented day.

totalSuppliedUsd.description: Supplied assets of the counted vaults, valued with bucket-aligned prices: EVK (escrow included) and, on rows written during the day, Securitize. A vault without a price that day is left out. Days before this rule shipped counted the published label set.

totalBorrowedUsd.description: Borrows of the counted EVK vaults, valued with bucket-aligned prices.

utilization.description: `totalBorrowedUsd / totalSuppliedUsd`, or zero when supplied is zero.

vaultCount.description: Counted EVK vaults with a value that day, escrow and empty vaults included. Earn and Securitize vaults are excluded so the definition is stable across captured and rebuilt rows. Days before this rule shipped counted the published label set.

earnTotalAssetsUsd.description: Current daily writes include Earn TVL; historical backfill rows are null because retained Earn history cannot reconstruct truthful USD values.

ProtocolStatsChainHistory.description: Retained history for one chain, restricted to the same eligible days as the aggregate. Explicitly selected chains without rows have empty history.

includePartial.description: Whether incomplete retained chain aggregates may appear in history.

groupBy.description: Present only when per-chain history is requested.

from.description: Effective inclusive range start in Unix seconds.

to.description: Effective inclusive range end in Unix seconds.

chainId.description: Canonical comma-separated selected chain IDs when filtering.

FlowsHistoryPointCoverage.description: Coverage of the selected configured chains for this day. Complete requires every selected chain row and all five category USD values; it does not assert complete historical event retention.

timestamp.description: UTC start of the represented day.

depositsUsd.description: Sum of retained EVK deposit asset amounts valued at event time, or null when unavailable.

withdrawalsUsd.description: Sum of retained EVK withdrawal asset amounts valued at event time, or null when unavailable.

borrowsUsd.description: Sum of retained EVK borrow asset amounts valued at event time, or null when unavailable.

repaysUsd.description: Sum of retained EVK repay asset amounts valued at event time, or null when unavailable.

liquidationsUsd.description: Sum of retained EVK liquidation repay asset amounts valued at event time, or null when unavailable.

netSuppliedUsd.description: DepositsUsd minus withdrawalsUsd; null if either input is unavailable. Borrows, repays and liquidations do not enter this formula. Negative values represent net withdrawals.

updatedAt.description: Oldest rollup calculation time across the selected chain rows, or null when a selected row or its calculation time is unavailable.

chainId.description: Canonical comma-separated selected chain IDs; without a filter, the served chains that run stats.

vault.description: Lowercase vault filter, present only for a vault-scoped request.

from.description: Effective inclusive range start in Unix seconds.

to.description: Effective inclusive range end in Unix seconds.

chainId.description: Chain ID for the returned chain-scoped aggregate.

OraclePriceRaw.description: Exact oracle quote values returned by contracts, represented as raw integer strings in the oracle unit-of-account scale.

amountIn.description: Raw input amount passed to the oracle.

accumulatedFeesShares.description: Raw accumulated fee shares as a bigint string.

accumulatedFeesAssets.description: Raw accumulated fee assets as a bigint string.

VaultCaps.description: EVK caps resolved to underlying asset base units as bigint strings. A vault without a cap (encoded zero) is `115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935` (type(uint256).max), with or without an on-chain read; `0` is a real zero cap.

supplyCap.description: Resolved supply cap as a bigint string in underlying asset base units; `115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935` when unlimited, `0` for a zero cap.

borrowCap.description: Resolved borrow cap as a bigint string in underlying asset base units; `115792089237316195423570985008687907853269984665640564039457584007913129639935` when unlimited, `0` for a zero cap.

status.description: Available when both liquidation legs have USD values, partial when one does, and unavailable when neither does.

source.description: Oracle USD enrichment is disabled by default and requires the LIQUIDATION_ORACLE_USD_ENABLED server rollout gate. Historical protocol oracle indicates that at least one missing USD leg uses the liquidation-block oracle quote. Token-denominated quotes require a USD snapshot from the preceding 15 minutes with no future block. Existing snapshot-valued legs are preserved.

reason.description: Present when valuation is partial or unavailable.

unitOfAccount.description: Debt vault unit-of-account address used by the protocol oracle.

repayValue.description: Debt repaid, quoted into the unit of account at the liquidation block.

collateralValue.description: Seized collateral-vault shares, quoted into the unit of account at the liquidation block.

bonusValue.description: Collateral value minus repay value in raw unit-of-account units.

repayAssets.description: Debt repaid in raw underlying units of the debt vault asset.

yieldBalance.description: Collateral seized in raw collateral-vault share units.

debtAsset.description: Underlying token address of the debt vault at the liquidation block.

debtAssetPriceUsd.description: Historical debt-asset USD price at or before the event time and block, never a current-price fallback.

collateralAsset.description: Underlying token address of the collateral vault at the liquidation block.

collateralAssetPriceUsd.description: Historical collateral-asset USD price at or before the event time and block, never a current-price fallback.

collateralAssets.description: Seized collateral shares converted to raw underlying units from the first indexed collateral VaultStatus after the liquidation log in the same transaction, using EVK virtual-deposit and rounding semantics. Null when that transaction-ordered status is unavailable.

collateralAssetsUsd.description: USD value of seized collateral. A liquidation-block oracle quote can value the seized shares when underlying token metadata or share conversion is unavailable; those native fields remain null.

bonusUsd.description: Collateral assets USD minus repaid debt USD. Null unless both values are available.

unitOfAccountValuation.description: Historical liquidation-block protocol-oracle quote used for fallback valuation. Retained when oracle enrichment completes the USD valuation. Null when no historical RPC quote was requested or available.

VaultInterestRates.description: Contract interest-rate values formatted as decimal strings in fraction units, not public percent APY numbers.

borrowSPY.description: Borrow rate per second as an exact decimal string.

borrowAPY.description: Borrow APY as an exact decimal fraction string; `1` means 100%.

supplyAPY.description: Supply APY as an exact decimal fraction string; `1` means 100%.

address.description: The adapter contract to evaluate; it need not be known to the registry.

source.description: `stored`: the registry already held the leg's verdict. `evaluated`: the leg was judged in this pass, at the same block. `unknown`: neither (deeper than two levels, or a cycle); the parent's cross-legs rule stays unknown.

OracleAdapterEvaluation.description: An evaluate-only verdict: the stored assessment's fields (`inActiveRoute` is false; `lastCheckedAt`, `schedulingTier` and `nextCheckAt` are null, since nothing is recorded) plus `persisted`, the pinned block hash and the legs judged on the way.

checksStatus.description: Health verdict of a recognized adapter. Always null for unrecognized adapters: identity and health are orthogonal, and no health claim is made about a contract whose getters are untrusted.

inActiveRoute.description: True when a current router configuration of a vault-backed router routes through this adapter, directly or as a cross-adapter leg. Refreshed hourly by the universe reconciler.

schedulingTier.description: Which periodic sweep re-checks the adapter: `active` (hourly) when a vault in the active tier prices through it (current router pairs, nested routers expanded, cross legs followed), `background` (daily) otherwise. updatedAt.description: When the row last changed. Rows written before it was recorded carry their creation time.

version.description: Opaque version of the row, `<updatedAt>|<changeId>`. Send it as `expectedVersion` with `POST /v3/changes` (domain `geo`, key the policy ID); a stale one records a superseded change instead of writing. Null on a derived row, which cannot be changed.

derivedFrom.description: Set on a row the server derives from a stored asset rule, null on a stored row. A derived row copies the rule's countries, type, reason and product or vault scope onto one token the app reaches that is built on an asset the rule selects (an ERC-4626 wrapper, an escrow, EVK or Earn share, an Earn allocation, a Pendle SY, PT, YT or LP). remove.description: Drop the collateral row instead of changing it.

resolvedVaults.description: `govSetResolvedVault(vault, resolved)` on the vault's router: the entry the lens would report after it (the vault, its asset, the unit of account, the unwrap chain) is added or removed, so a route staged in the same batch on the vault's asset prices it. A vault with an adapter configured for itself keeps answering through it either way, as the router reads the configured pair before any resolution.

quote.description: Defaults to the vault's unit of account.

VaultConsistencyContext.description: The findings behind a Layer 2 verdict, for the policies that grade more than ownership. An Earn vault's: whether each strategy it can hold funds in (a cap or a withdraw-queue slot) and each active collateral of those strategies is escrow or shown (claimed, assigned to a product, not suspended in its own Layer 2 check, and passing Layer 1 when the vault's entity claims it), gating always for the vault entity's own and, for another curator's, only until acceptable after the curator's latest cap increase; a deprecated one only warns. And whether its owner, unless renounced, and its curator, when one is set, are addresses an entity registers. Null for every other vault, and for an Earn vault suspended on ownership whose Earn state could not be read; replaced by each completed Layer 2 check. The first required failure is `consistencyReason`; a failed advisory badges the vault `warning`.

x-finding-key-namespaces.description: One per strategy in scope; <address> is the lowercase strategy vault address. `observed.link` is `{ phase, committedAtBlock, committedAtLogIndex, acceptedAt }`. `own` (claimed by the vault's entity) and `admission` (not acceptable since the curator's latest cap increase) gate; `accepted`, `drift` (failing after acceptance, or a collateral activated after the increase) and `uncapped` (cap zero) do not.
One per active collateral of those strategies; <address> is the lowercase collateral vault address.

A pending change graded by the rule it will face once accepted, a strategy a pending cap adds, a collateral it brings, or an owner transfer awaiting acceptance. Never required, so outside `outcome`, `consistencyStatus` and visibility. `observed` is `{ pending, validAt, submittedAtBlock }`; `validAt` is null for an owner transfer.

cause.description: Why this is not a pass. On `fail` and `unknown` it is the failure; on `not_applicable` it is why the rule did not run, and its absence on an `evidence.*` row is what separates a skipped check from an observation. The rule key alone cannot say: `hooks.zero-or-trusted` fails either because the hook target is untrusted or because a zero target disabled an exit operation, and those have opposite remedies. Switch on `code`; `subject` is the value to act on; `summary` is one sentence naming it, and is what `configReason` carries for the blocking finding.

subject.description: The one value to act on -- an address, or a formatted parameter value. Null when the rule names none.

summary.description: One sentence naming the value that failed, not the requirement it failed.

remedy.description: Which way out applies. Null when the answer is not the reader's to act on.

before.description: The stored finding; null when the preview introduces the key.

after.description: The previewed finding; null when the change removes the key.

VaultAssessmentPreview.description: What a fresh Layer 1 check would say, in the shape of the vault's kind: `family` names the variant. EVK previews may carry applied overrides and findings whose simulation could not run; Earn and Securitize previews accept no overrides and answer both lists empty. Each variant lists the finding keys its policy can produce.

appliedOverrides.description: Always empty; this vault kind accepts no overrides.

notSimulated.description: Always empty; nothing is simulated for this vault kind.

appliedOverrides.description: Always empty; this vault kind accepts no overrides.

notSimulated.description: Always empty; nothing is simulated for this vault kind.

VaultAssessmentPreviewBase.description: The fields every preview answers, whatever the vault kind.

currentConfigStatus.description: The stored Layer 1 status, `unverified` when nothing is stored yet.

configStatusIfApplied.description: The status the stored check would write from `currentConfigStatus` and the previewed outcome.

checksStatus.description: What the advisory findings would say if this configuration were applied. Same axis as `checksStatus` on the stored assessment.

changed.description: Findings whose verdict differs from the stored assessment, added and removed ones included.

appliedOverrides.description: One line per override applied, in the order applied.

notSimulated.description: Finding keys left unknown because their simulation could not run: a quote the probe could not reach, or `oracle.adapters-recognized` when the evaluate-only check refused a proposed adapter. Each finding names the reason in `observed`; the list is empty when every change the batch makes was simulated.

localOutcome.description: Verdict excluding collateral-recognition findings; used for cycle-safe recognition.

checksStatus.description: Health of the advisory findings, orthogonal to the gating verdict in `configStatus`: the rules that disclose a curator's judgment call rather than suspend a vault. Null when the policy emitted no advisory finding. Same axis and vocabulary as an oracle adapter's `checksStatus`; a vault advisory never condemns, so this does not reach `negative`.

key.description: Stable rule key. Static keys are listed in `x-finding-keys`; the templated namespaces are described in `x-finding-key-namespaces`. `evidence.*` keys are observations that never gate the verdict, but they are not the only non-gating findings: read `required` for that (`irm.max-apy` is advisory). A `scheduled.` key grades a pending timelocked change and never counts toward the verdict, `checksStatus`, `summary` or visibility. A required key ending in `.recognized` is a cross-entity recognition rule excluded from `localOutcome`. Keys are never renamed, only added.

x-finding-key-namespaces.description: One group per active collateral of an EVK market vault; <address> is the lowercase collateral vault address. `recognized` reads the collateral's `localOutcome`.

One group per active strategy of an Earn vault; <address> is the lowercase strategy vault address. `recognized` reads the strategy's full `outcome`, or its `localOutcome` when the strategy is itself an Earn vault. It is required until the strategy has passed after the curator's latest cap increase and advisory after, or while the vault caps it at zero; `observed.link` is `{ phase, committedAtBlock, committedAtLogIndex, acceptedAt }`.

A timelocked change submitted on an Earn vault and not yet live, graded by the rule it will face once accepted, a strategy a pending cap adds or a pending timelock decrease. Never required, and outside `outcome`, `checksStatus`, `summary` and visibility. `observed` is `{ pending, validAt, submittedAtBlock }`, `pending` holding what the live rule would observe; a cause's summary starts with when the change can be accepted.

required.description: Whether the finding gates the verdict. Required findings reduce into `outcome` and `localOutcome`; an advisory finding carries a real `pass`, `fail` or `unknown` outcome for the reader but never suspends the vault.

cause.description: Why this is not a pass. On `fail` and `unknown` it is the failure; on `not_applicable` it is why the rule did not run, and its absence on an `evidence.*` row is what separates a skipped check from an observation. The rule key alone cannot say: `hooks.zero-or-trusted` fails either because the hook target is untrusted or because a zero target disabled an exit operation, and those have opposite remedies. Switch on `code`; `subject` is the value to act on; `summary` is one sentence naming it, and is what `configReason` carries for the blocking finding.

subject.description: The one value to act on -- an address, or a formatted parameter value. Null when the rule names none.

summary.description: One sentence naming the value that failed, not the requirement it failed.

remedy.description: Which way out applies. Null when the answer is not the reader's to act on.

exempted.description: True when a platform rule exemption downgraded this finding to evidence.

configStatus.description: Layer 1 (on-chain configuration safety) lifecycle. `unverified`: never verified, or the first check failed (`configContext.outcome` is `fail`). `verified`: the configuration policy passed. `suspended`: a re-check failed after the vault had been verified. `revoked`: set manually by a platform admin. `pending`: a platform admin requested a re-check through the PATCH endpoint; the automatic loop never writes this value. A due check is signalled by a non-null `configCheckAt`, not by the status, and a passing status is left unchanged while re-checks run.

checksStatus.description: Health of the advisory findings, orthogonal to the gating verdict in `configStatus`: the rules that disclose a curator's judgment call rather than suspend a vault. Null when the policy emitted no advisory finding. Same axis and vocabulary as an oracle adapter's `checksStatus`; a vault advisory never condemns, so this does not reach `negative`.

configCheckAt.description: When the next Layer 1 check is due. Non-null means an on-chain change or a manual request is awaiting a check; cleared when the check completes.

configLastCheckedAt.description: When Layer 1 last completed a check, whatever the outcome.

configFailedAttempts.description: Layer 1 checks that failed to finish since the last completed one: the RPC was unreachable, or a read the policy needs was not answered. Each failure pushes the next check back, from 5 minutes and doubling up to 6 hours; an on-chain change still triggers a check at once. Back to 0 when a check completes.

configLastFailedAt.description: When the latest of those failures happened; null once a check completes.

schedulingTier.description: Which periodic sweep re-checks the vault. `active` (hourly): labeled and not deprecated in the latest published version, or total supply worth at least 100,000 USD, or a collateral or Earn strategy of such a vault; Layer 1's verdict plays no part, so a hidden vault stays hourly. `background` (daily): everything else. `static` (never swept): escrow vaults, whose configuration cannot change. Governance events trigger an immediate check whatever the tier. On a chain this deployment does not index the tier is the stored default and `nextCheckAt` is null: no sweep reaches the row.

nextCheckAt.description: When the next Layer 1 check is expected: `configCheckAt` when a check is scheduled, else the last check plus the tier's sweep interval; null for a vault never checked with nothing scheduled, and for a static vault with nothing scheduled.

configVerifiedAt.description: When the vault last passed Layer 1.

consistencyStatus.description: Layer 2 (label to chain consistency) lifecycle. `not_applicable`: nothing to check (escrow or unclaimed vault). `verified`: the labels agree with the current on-chain governor or owner and with product membership, and an Earn vault's required `consistencyContext` findings pass. `suspended`: an inconsistency was detected, such as a governor outside the entity's addresses, a product mixing governed and ungoverned vaults, or an Earn vault's unclaimed dependency or unregistered owner or curator; resolution is a platform-admin action. `revoked`: set manually by a platform admin. `pending`: a re-check was requested manually, or the first check could not read chain state and will retry.

consistencyReason.description: The Layer 2 verdict in one sentence, for display. For a `suspended` Earn vault it is the `cause.summary` of the first required finding that failed. The findings themselves, with their keys and outcomes, are in `consistencyContext`; key on those, not on this sentence.

consistencyCheckAt.description: When the next Layer 2 check is due. Set by governance events on chain and by manual requests, and for an Earn vault also by configuration events of the vault, its strategies and their collaterals, by label publications that change a dependency's standing, and by registration changes of its owner or curator; label mutations run their check synchronously instead.

consistencyLastCheckedAt.description: When Layer 2 last completed a check, whatever the outcome.

riskStatus.description: Layer 3 (risk context) lifecycle. Not yet automated: no worker writes this field, so it stays `unverified` unless a platform admin sets it through the PATCH endpoint.

tags.description: Platform-managed tags. Every tag outside the curator vocabulary lives here (`recently added`, the Base app's `base`); vault reads union them with the label row's vocabulary tags.

platformUpdatedAt.description: When a platform admin (or the label import) last wrote this assessment; null while the vault has no stored assessment. The checks never move it. The ETag of GET and PATCH is this value quoted.

checks.description: Decision evidence: `decidedBy`, `reason`, layer statuses, the resolved deprecation, the platform `notExplorable*` overrides as authored, and `listing` — the effective per-side discovery result (`{ lend: { hidden, decidedBy }, borrow: { hidden, decidedBy } }`) after platform overrides, curator flags, and deprecation.

Error404ChainCapability.description: Not found, or `CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED`: a requested chain does not run the capability the operation needs (see `capabilities` on `/v3/chains`), named in `x-chain-capability` or, where it depends on the request, in the parameter. `details.chainIds` lists those chains and `details.capability` names the capability.

LabelContextNotFound.description: The label set or version could not be resolved: `labelSet` names no label set, `version` matches no published key or alias, or a `current` or `draft` read names a set other than `public`. This is the only 404 of the label reads that carries `details.labelSet` and `details.version`, which echo the request; a missing row never does, so a client can tell "this label set or version does not exist" from "this row is not labelled".

Retry-After.description: Seconds until next request is allowed.
