post.description:
Publishes an immutable snapshot of entity, product, and vault-label content.
Geo policies remain live and are not included. The snapshot builder decides
per row where the content comes from: a full publish takes every draft row
that no hold covers and keeps held rows at their published content; a
partial publish (`selection` in the body, platform session only) takes the
selected rows and whatever they need for a consistent version, overriding
holds for those rows, and keeps everything else as published. Left-out
changes stay pending for the timer. A draft vault row with no labels (the
row discovery materialises for every vault it finds, a claim cleared) is not
label content: no publication takes it, a selection naming one is a no-op,
and the `report.leftOut` says how many such rows the draft holds and which
the selection named. The `report` also lists what went live, what
was pulled in, what a hold kept back and why, and which holds were
overridden. `?dryRun=true` returns the report without writing anything.
When the built content matches the latest published version, the endpoint
returns that version with `publishOutcome: unchanged` and does not create a
release. Accepts a platform session or an API key holding the
`labels:publish` capability; a key may only publish in full. The version
records which kind of actor published it, and every publication is audited.
To publish exactly what a dry run showed, send its `draftToken` as
`expectedDraftToken`: if the draft, the latest version or the holds a partial
publish would override moved since, the answer is 412 with `details.reason`
`draft-changed` and the current `details.draftToken`, and nothing is written.
Without the field, the publish takes the draft as it is at that moment; it
will become required for keys, and a key publish without it is logged.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Build the version and return the report without publishing.

expectedDraftToken.description: The `draftToken` of the dry run this publish confirms. Ignored on a dry run. Optional for now; keys will have to send it.

200.description: Publishable label content is unchanged and the latest version is returned, or the request was a dry run and only the report is returned.

412.description: `expectedDraftToken` no longer matches: what this publish would write moved since the dry run. `details.reason` is `draft-changed` and `details.draftToken` is the current token. Nothing was written; preview again before publishing.

The part of the publication state a curator surface needs to say when
a draft change goes live: the publication mode, whether automatic
publication is suspended, the pending due time, and the latest
published version. Carries no reason, no actor, and no revision, so it
is readable with an entity session or without one. In `manual` mode
`dueAt` is always null: changes go live when the platform publishes.
Responses are private and never cached.

post.description:
Screens an EVM address using TRM and the versioned Euler policy. The endpoint
requires an active, unexpired API key with the `compliance:screen`
capability, or a platform session whose operator is on the admin allowlist
(the Toolbox, with the CSRF header); a session also receives the matched rules,
the evaluation id, its expiry and the retained provider payload. It applies a
dedicated per-caller limit of 100 requests per minute by default. Results can reuse
a fresh evaluation for the configured window (24 hours by default), while every
capability-authorized request, including requests rejected before provider screening,
is retained in the screening audit history. The service fails closed with 503 when screening cannot
produce a trustworthy result or when production enablement is off, and the two are told apart by
the error code rather than the status: `SERVICE_DISABLED` with `details.reason: disabled` means this
deployment carries no provider, so retrying can never succeed, while `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with
`details.reason: unavailable` is a configured provider that failed and is worth retrying.

get.description:
Pages through the retained provider evaluations, newest first, including
the raw provider payload and the screened address. Requires an active,
unexpired API key with the `compliance:screening-read`
capability, a separate grant from `compliance:screen`, or a platform
session whose operator is on the admin allowlist (the Toolbox).
Responses are compliance data: `Cache-Control: no-store`, never log them.
`suspicious=true|false` keeps one verdict. A query parameter this route does not
list answers 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

Pages through the append-only request audit log, newest first: which key
asked, for which address and chain, whether a cached evaluation was
reused, and how rejected or failed requests ended. Requires the
`compliance:screening-read` capability or an allowlisted platform
session. Responses are compliance data: `Cache-Control: no-store`,
never log them. The log records no verdict, so there is no `suspicious`
filter here: it answers 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, like any query parameter
this route does not list.

windows. Requires the `compliance:screening-read` capability or an
allowlisted platform session.

get.description:
Every unreleased hold: quarantines raised by the reviewer and entity holds
raised by entity suspension. Accepts a platform session or a key with
`labels:reject` or `labels:draft-read`. Actor identities are returned to
platform sessions only. Only the `public` label set has holds.

post.description:
Rejects one entity, product, or vault-label row: the curator's draft stays
intact, the row keeps its published content on every full publish, and the
hash of the draft content at the time is recorded so a later edit is
detectable. The row must exist in the draft or in the latest published
version. Accepts a platform session or a key with `labels:reject`. One
active quarantine per row; a repeat answers 409 with the existing hold.
Send `expectedContentHash` to hold only the revision that was reviewed: a
draft that moved since answers 412 `stale-review` and writes no hold and no
event. It will become required for keys.

delete.description:
Releases one quarantine so the next full publish takes the row's draft.
Accepts a platform session or a key with `labels:reject`. Entity holds are
released by resuming the entity and answer 409 here. `expectedContentHash`
releases only the revision that was reviewed; a draft that moved since
answers 412 `stale-review` and nothing is released. It will become required
for keys.

parameters.name: expectedContentHash
parameters.description: The held row's draft revision the reviewer judged, the change log's `afterContentHash`. To name a row the draft no longer has, use POST `…/release` with `expectedContentHash: null`.

post.summary: Release a quarantine with a reason
post.description:
Releases one quarantine like DELETE on the hold, and records an optional
`reason` on the hold (`releaseReason`) and in the publication event. An empty
body releases with no reason. Accepts a platform session or a key with
`labels:reject`. Entity holds are released by resuming the entity and answer
409 here. `expectedContentHash` releases only the revision that was reviewed;
a draft that moved since answers 412 `stale-review` and nothing is released.

get.description:
One row per label mutation with the actor, the before and after content,
and the changed fields, written in the row's own transaction. `pending`
rows wait for a publish, `published` rows name the version that carried
them, `quarantined` rows are held, and `superseded` rows were replaced by a
later change to the same row. Newest first. Accepts a platform session or a
key with `labels:draft-read`, `labels:reject`, or `labels:publish`; actor
identities and request ids are returned to platform sessions only. Only the
`public` label set has a change log.

post.summary: Preview the Layer 1 verdict of a EVK vault, for the live configuration or a proposed one
post.description:
Answers what a fresh Layer 1 check would say, without storing anything. With an empty body
(or no body) it is a fresh check of the live vault under its policy family; with
`overrides` it is the EVK policy judging the live snapshot with the proposed configuration
applied: caps, LTV rows (change, add, remove), the interest rate model (its rates re-probed
with the vault impersonated at the pinned block), router resolutions (`resolvedVaults`),
oracle routes (base to adapter; a proposed adapter's verdict comes from the registry when
it knows it and from the evaluate-only adapter check when it does not, and every quote a
changed route or resolution answers is simulated through the proposed adapter at the pinned
block, one unit of the base converted through the resolved vaults the way the router
converts it) and the hook configuration. The answer names the findings whose verdict
differs from the stored assessment (`changed`), the status the vault would land on
(`configStatusIfApplied`, from `currentConfigStatus` and the outcome) and, in
`notSimulated`, the findings left unknown because their simulation could not run (the
chain unreachable for a quote, the evaluate-only adapter check refused), each naming the
reason in its `observed`. Platform rule exemptions apply as the
stored check applies them. One vault is previewed at most 6 times per minute (429 with
`Retry-After`) and the reads get 12 seconds (504). Accepts a platform session or a
API key holding `assessments:evaluate`; a curator session is never enough.

Needs the `assessments` chain capability; a chain without it answers 404
`CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED`.

422.description: The body fails validation (`error.details.issues`), or overrides were sent for a vault outside the EVK family (`error.details.family`).

429.description: The vault was previewed more than 6 times in the last minute; `Retry-After` says when to retry.

504.description: The on-chain reads did not finish within the 12-second budget (`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`).

get.description:
Returns lending aggregates across the selected chains. The stats count what the app shows, plus the vaults kept out of it only by deprecation, for every vault from Euler's factories (the EVK factory, escrow vaults included; the Earn factory; the Securitize factory). Shown means the verdict is `visible` or `warning` with at least one listing side not hidden, as the app and the work items read it, so Layer 1, Layer 2, advisories, claims and listing flags apply exactly as in the app. An escrow or Securitize vault counts while a counted vault accepts it as collateral with a liquidation LTV above zero, even when Layer 1 hides it. Vaults hidden by checks, hidden by a platform admin or a curator verdict, pending review, unclaimed, or without a Layer 1 verdict yet are left out. Prices are the selected current price at most 24 hours old, the on-chain fallback included. A vault that holds a balance without such a price, or whose balance was read more than 15 minutes ago, is left out and its chain still counts with what was priced, however much of the chain that vault holds. `meta.excludedVaults` reports what was left out and why. `earnTotalAssetsUsd` is reported separately and is not part of `totalSuppliedUsd` or `utilization`. Chains with incomplete membership or stale source state are omitted and reported in response metadata; a chain with unread balances still contributes the vaults it read. Partial responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`.
Needs the `stats` chain capability. A `chainId` naming a chain without it answers 404 `CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED`; without `chainId`, served chains without it are left out and listed in `meta.excludedChains`.

get.summary: Daily protocol or selected-chain lending history
get.description:
Days written from this release on count the vaults `/v3/protocol/stats` counts; earlier days keep the earlier rule and are not recomputed. A row written after its day closed (catch-up, repair, backfill) has no daily Securitize balances, so it leaves Securitize deposits out, and a backfill row has no Earn total. A day is written with what was priced: a vault without a usable price that day is left out, and the day stays as written. Returns complete retained daily aggregates by default. With includePartial=true, days with only some chain rows are also returned with explicit point coverage and Cache-Control no-store. Missing dates and per-metric availability are reported in meta.coverage in either mode. Empty scopes remain empty; no zero-valued days are synthesized. Only 1d resolution is supported, ranges are inclusive, the default window is 30 days, and the maximum is 732 buckets. With groupBy=chain, data.chains adds chain-ID-ordered series from the same database snapshot and eligible days as data.history. Additive EVK values reconcile to the aggregate; utilization is a ratio, not a sum. Without an explicit chain filter, groups contain retained chain IDs only, not an inferred historical registry.
Needs the `stats` chain capability. A `chainId` naming a chain without it answers 404 `CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED`; without `chainId` the stored protocol series is read, and served chains without `stats` are listed in `meta.excludedChains`.

parameters.description: Add per-chain series with independent range and metric coverage.

parameters.name: includePartial
parameters.description: Include retained healthy-chain subtotals on incomplete days. Does not reconstruct missing vaults or chains.

chains.description: Present only with groupBy=chain. Sorted by numeric chain ID, with history ordered by ascending UTC day.

get.summary: Daily EVK supplied net flows and event-category USD totals
get.description:
Returns retained daily EVK deposit, withdrawal, borrow, repay and liquidation USD totals. Net supplied flow is depositsUsd minus withdrawalsUsd; borrows, repays and liquidations are reported separately and do not enter the net formula. Each category is independently nullable; missing chain rows or unavailable category valuation are not reported as zero. Net supplied flow remains available when deposits and withdrawals are available even if another category is not. Values use eligible positive historical asset prices at or before each event, within 15 minutes and bounded by the event block. Rollups and backfills cover retained raw EVK events; coverage describes the requested range and does not prove complete historical source retention. Protocol, chain and vault scopes use the current visible labelled EVK vault membership; Earn and unlabelled vaults are excluded. Historical label membership is not reconstructed. Omitting chainId selects the served chains that run stats. A vault filter requires exactly one selected chain. Only 1d resolution is supported, ranges are inclusive, the default window is 30 days, and the maximum is 732 buckets. Only closed UTC days are published; the current open day is omitted. With groupBy=chain, data.chains adds a series and independent coverage for every selected chain, including empty series. Missing days remain absent; no zero-valued days are synthesized. Incomplete range coverage uses Cache-Control no-store. Complete HTTP responses may remain cached for up to 300 seconds after source invalidation; fresh database reads exclude pending buckets, including after the cached response expires. Unknown or repeated query parameters, duplicate chain IDs and invalid ranges return 400. An unsupported chainId returns 404 with error code CHAIN_NOT_SUPPORTED.
Needs the `stats` chain capability. A `chainId` naming a chain without it answers 404 `CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED`; without `chainId`, served chains without it are left out and listed in `meta.excludedChains`.

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: Add series ordered by numeric chain ID, each ordered by ascending UTC day.

in the stored assessment's shape. Nothing is written: no registry row, no assessment; the
adapter is recorded when a router installs it (the indexer's `ConfigSet` handler) or when
the hourly router-history sweep finds it. Cross-adapter legs the registry does not know
are evaluated inline at the same block, two levels deep, and reported in `legs`; Pyth
reads carry a fresh Hermes update like the stored checks. The address must have bytecode
on the chain (422 otherwise), one address is evaluated at most 6 times per minute (429 with
`Retry-After`), a repeated request within 30 seconds answers the same evaluation, and the
on-chain reads are given 12 seconds (504 when exceeded). Accepts a platform session or a
API key holding `assessments:evaluate`; a curator session is never enough.

`CHAIN_CAPABILITY_DISABLED`.

GraphQL endpoint (shared auth/rate limit with REST), proxied to the
Ponder GraphQL API.
Ponder LIKE filter operators reject unescaped `%` and `_` wildcard values.
Before proxying, the API bounds the complete request including unused runtime variables,
variable defaults, inline arguments, input bytes/nodes/depth, boolean clauses, list entries,
aliases, `totalCount`, execution cost, `limit` (default maximum 1,000), and `offset`
(default maximum 10,000). Offset scan cost is `offset + limit`; selected output expansion
remains based on `limit`. Resource violations return `QUERY_TOO_BROAD` and malformed
documents return `VALIDATION_ERROR` without contacting Ponder. Ponder 0.15.17 does not use

Each API process also enforces a shared upstream concurrency cap (default 8), one total
fetch-and-stream timeout (default 10 seconds), redirect rejection, GraphQL JSON media-type
and object-shape validation, and a streamed decoded response cap (default 5,242,880 bytes).
A non-queueing per-process query-cost bucket defaults to 100,000 units of capacity and a
25,000-unit-per-second refill. Exhaustion returns 429 before an upstream slot is acquired;
the shared per-client API rate limiter remains the outer control.

`X-Chain-Id`, then the JSON body `chainId`, in that precedence order.

get.description:
`token-logo-missing` requires `token-images:read` or an allowlisted Toolbox session. It returns in-scope assets (an asset of a vault the app shows, or of a collateral such a vault accepts) on enabled chains without a managed image, excluding applied removals and dismissals, with the worker's latest outcome, provider, attempt time and next retry time when available, and returns 503 until legacy occupancy is verified and source cutover is enabled. Scope inputs may be up to a minute old. With `state=reviewed` it lists dismissals instead.

`token-price-missing` requires `price-sources:read` or an allowlisted Toolbox session. It is computed on each read for every in-scope asset (an asset of a vault the app shows) that is not priced, ordered by priority, then by deposits in USD at the last price. Inputs other than reviews may be up to a minute old; a dismissal or resume shows on the next read. A proposed dismissal leaves the item outstanding until an admin approves it.

`asset-newly-exposed` requires `geo:read` or an allowlisted Toolbox session. It lists every asset a vault users can act on reaches, read from the exposure sweep (every 15 minutes): the assets of every EVK, Earn and Securitize vault that is not deprecated, verified or not, explorable or not; the assets of the collaterals the shown vaults accept; and what those are built on. A rule covers an asset when one of its asset selectors picks the asset, or picks a token the asset is built on; a rule limited to one product or vault leaves the item outstanding and is named in `rules`. Ordered by priority (exposure), then deposits in USD, then the newest exposure. `state` is, first match wins, `covered` (a rule applies on the whole chain), `reviewed` (a standing review), `baseline` (exposed when the chain's first sweep ran, so an existing asset is never new), `unverified-only` (reached only through vaults the app does not show) or `new`. The default `outstanding` is `new` only, and only `new` items count in the open-items gauge; `baseline` and `unverified-only` items are listed and reviewable with their own `state`.

Each `asset-newly-exposed` item carries `coverage`, an onboarding checklist of five decisions: logo, price, category (`tags`), intrinsic APY (`yield`) and geo. A piece is settled when it has its data, an automatic match, or an applied "none" review; a settled piece is never a need. `needs` keeps the items with a need in any of the named pieces: not settled, no open proposal, in scope and not paused. Each piece has its write path, with no route of its own: logo: `POST /v3/changes/uploads` then a `token-images` `fill` (or a verified `fill` with `trustedSource`, or a PT `derive`) on `POST /v3/changes`; "none": `POST /v3/work-items/token-logo-missing/{id}/dismiss` with `no-logo-available`. price: a `price-sources` change on `POST /v3/changes` (key `<source>/<chainId>:<address>`); "none": `POST /v3/work-items/token-price-missing/{id}/dismiss` with `onchain-only` or `no-price-source`. tags: a `token-tags` change on `POST /v3/changes` (key `<tag>:<ruleType>:<value>`; the `addresses` rule type tags one token, value `<chainId>:<address>`); "none": `POST /v3/work-items/token-category-missing/{id}/dismiss` with `no-category`. yield: a `yield-sources` change (key `<source>/<chainId>:<address>`) or a `yield-pools` change (key `<chainId>:<address>`) on `POST /v3/changes`; "none": `POST /v3/work-items/token-intrinsic-apy-missing/{id}/dismiss` with `no-intrinsic-apy`. geo: the `/v3/geo-policies` routes or a `geo` change on `POST /v3/changes`; "none": `POST /v3/work-items/asset-newly-exposed/{id}/dismiss` with `no-rule-needed`. `token-category-missing` and `token-intrinsic-apy-missing` have no list of their own: this route returns 400 for them.

For every type, `review.decidedBy` is null for API-key readers. A missing or unknown `type` returns 400 before any capability check.

For `token-logo-missing`, reviewed lists dismissals: in-scope tokens without a logo that carry an applied dismissal, each with its `review` (`WorkItemReview`). `asset-newly-exposed` also accepts `all`, `new`, `baseline`, `unverified-only` and `covered`; its `outstanding` is `new` only, with or without `needs`.

post.summary: Submit a change in any registered domain
post.description: One body for every domain, token images included; an API key must send `evidence`. A key needs the domain's `:propose` or `:write` capability; the server computes the op class, runs its checks and decides with the domain policy, and an active suspension turns an auto-apply into a proposal. A stale `expectedVersion` records a superseded change; the same actor's open proposal on the target is superseded by the new one. A token keeps one intrinsic APY source. A `yield-sources` or `yield-pools` change that turns an entry on, as an add or an enable, returns 409 with `details.reason` `one-apy-source` while the token has another enabled yield source or DefiLlama pool, or is a Pendle PT that has not matured; `details.apySources` names the other source and the message says how to switch. This holds for every actor, platform sessions included. A key's proposal is refused at submit, and an approval or a revert that would turn a second source on is refused the same way. Disabling, removing or editing a source is always allowed. To switch, send the new source and the change that disables or removes the old one together to `POST /v3/changes/batch`. A platform session's `dismiss` applies only while the work list's dismiss rule holds, and returns 409 otherwise; a key's dismissal is a proposal, checked again when an admin approves it. A geo `update` or `remove` must name a stored rule; a derived address row from `GET /v3/geo-policies` cannot be changed and returns 404. A price-sources `fill` from a key or a system actor applies on its own only when every fill check passes, `provider-fresh` included, which needs the provider's own time for its price (CoinGecko `last_updated_at`, DefiLlama `timestamp`, Pyth `publish_time`, or for an ERC-4626 share the time of the underlying's stored V3 price) to be at most 24 hours old and at most 5 minutes ahead. An ERC-4626 fill also needs `asset()` to be the identifier, any decimals override to equal the chain's, and the underlying to have a positive V3 price, taken as V3 selects it from any source, the on-chain fallback and other shares included. Pendle gives no price time; its price is a current quote, so the time of the read stands for it. A Pendle fill applies on its own only for the PT itself, when V3 has a Pendle market for it on a chain the Pendle price source supports and Pendle prices it above 0; a matured PT that Pendle still prices qualifies, at its redemption value. A Pyth source never applies on its own. When a provider or the chain cannot answer for a fill that could apply on its own (no current entry, a CoinGecko, DefiLlama, ERC-4626 or Pendle source, not disabled, from a key with `price-sources:write` or a system actor, and no active suspension), the change is not recorded and the request returns 503; send it again later. Any other change is recorded as a proposal with the failed checks. For token images, dispatches permissions by registered domain. `token-images:propose` permits staged candidates and `token-images:write` permits a verified CoinGecko or Pendle fill. Replacements and removals always remain proposals. The `derive` operation builds a Pendle PT's logo server-side from the current managed image of the token named in the optional `value.source` (by default the PT's recorded underlying in `token_integrations`), as a circle crop with the teal `#17e3c2` PT ring, recorded with `derivedFrom` (source digest) in its `derive-source` check. A platform session applies a derive; a system actor applies only an empty-slot fill from the recorded underlying's verified-provider image; any other derive is a proposal. A target that is not a Pendle PT returns 400; a source without a managed image, or one that already carries the ring, returns 409. A verified fill requires an eligible token class, empty managed slot, exact chain-and-contract provider match, and verified legacy cutover. Incomplete cutover or provider unavailability returns 503. API-key responses omit operator attribution. The generic change has expected/resulting versions and database decision order; token image snapshots and provider evidence are stored in a domain detail record.

post.summary: Review a work item ("reviewed, no action")
post.description: The same route for every work list. An allowlisted Toolbox session with CSRF records an applied review. An API key with the domain's `:propose` or `:write` capability records a proposed review, which an admin approves in the Changes inbox; machine actors must send `evidence`. The kind must be one the work list recognizes, or null to stop for now: a null-kind price review lapses like `no-price-source`, a null-kind logo review holds until resumed, a null-kind geo review lapses when the asset is exposed again. A geo review needs `geo:propose` or `geo:write` from a key. `token-category-missing` records `no-category` in `token-tags` and `token-intrinsic-apy-missing` records `no-intrinsic-apy` in `yield-sources`, keyed `<chainId>:<address>`; neither takes a null kind. 409 when a standing review exists, or, for an admin, when another admin's review landed first. A proposed review leaves the item outstanding.
